title: Characteristics of Precipitation-formed Polyethylene Glycol Microgels Are Controlled by Molecular Weight of Reactants
protocol: Prepare a 0.5% photoinitiator solution by dissolving photoinitiator in deionized water.
Filter the photoinitiator solution through a 0.22 μm filter.
Store the filtered photoinitiator solution at 4 °C in the dark.
Heat PBS tablet to dissolve it completely in 1 L of deionized water.
Filter the prepared PBS solution through a 0.22 μm filter.
Store the filtered PBS solution at 4 °C.
Measure 612 μl of triethanolamine and preheat it to 37 °C.
Add 612 μl of triethanolamine and 260 μl of 6 M HCl to 39.4 ml of PBS (pH=7.4).
Adjust the pH of the buffer solution to approximately 7.8 using additional HCl or NaOH if necessary.
Filter the adjusted buffer solution through a 0.22 μm filter.
Store the filtered and adjusted buffer solution at 37 °C.
Weigh out PEG-DA and add PBS/TEOA/HCl buffer to final concentration of 200 mg/ml.
Add PBS/TEOA/HCl buffer slowly to control PEG concentration carefully.
Dissolve Na2SO4 in DI H2O for a 1.5 M solution.
Heat the sodium sulfate solution until Na2SO4 is completely dissolved.
Filter the sodium sulfate solution through a 0.22 μm filter as necessary.
Place 127.5 μl of PBS/TEOA/HCl buffer into tubes where microgels will be formed.
Add 10 μl of 0.5% photoinitiator to the tubes.
Add 25 μl of 200 mg/ml PEG solution to the tubes.
Heat these tubes along with the sodium sulfate solution to 37 °C.
Mix the tubes while heating.
Add the desired molecule to the PBS/TEOA/HCl buffer, photoinitiator, and PEG solution for encapsulation.
Mix tube containing the mixture by pipetting 3-5 times or wait 30 seconds after adding 87.5 μl of 1.5 M Na2SO4.
Place the tube under UV light and crosslink for 30 seconds.
Add 750 μl PBS to form a pellet upon centrifugation and mix well.
Wash microgels 5 times by centrifuging at 4,000 x g for 2 minutes and exchanging the supernatant with PBS without disturbing the microgel pellet.
Pipette 30 μl of microgels from the pellet into 1 ml DI H2O.
Sonicate the microgel solution in a water bath sonicator for 1 hour at 50-60 Hz and 1.4 A or mix vigorously to suspend the microgels.
Pipette 15 μl of the microgel solution onto a clean glass slide.
Put a #1.5 cover slip on top of the slide.
Flip the slide and cover slip over onto a laboratory tissue.
Push down on the slide to remove excess solution and ensure that the microgels are in a single layer.
Capture several images of the microgels using a DIC 100X oil objective.
Measure the microgels to obtain a representative diameter.
Calculate PDI using the volume-based equation where N is the total number of microgels and Vi is the volume of microgel i.
Prepare dextran solutions in DI H2O at concentrations of 7%, 6%, 5%, 4%, 3%, and 1% (w/v).
Add 1 ml of 7% dextran solution to a 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Slowly pipette 1 ml of 6% dextran solution to form a distinct layer atop the 7% dextran.
Wait 5 min then add 1 ml of the 5% dextran solution.
Continue until all dextran solutions are layered in order of decreasing concentration.
Carefully layer the microgels above the 1% dextran solution.
Centrifuge the gradient for 10 min at 4,000 x g and 5 °C.
Wash the microgels 5 times in DI H2O.
Swell the washed microgels for a minimum of 48 hours in preweighed microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the swollen microgels at 4,000 x g for 10 minutes.
Remove all supernatant and record the wet mass.
Use filtering methods to ensure all excess water is removed.
Freeze the microgels at -80 °C.
Lyophilize the frozen microgels to constant mass to obtain the dry mass.
Calculate the water content in the microgels using Water% = (Ms - Md) / Md x 100.
Determine polymer content by Polymer% = 100 - Water%.
